messages:
Maya Chen: Heads-up — planning cutover for Dedicated customer Orion Labs to release v5.2 tonight. Target window 18:00–19:00 UTC. Canary plan: start 10% for 15m, ramp to 50% over 30m, then full if healthy. Need go/no-go by 17:30 UTC. Also note a KMS key rotation was scheduled earlier today — confirm no collision with vault keys for the tenant.

DeployBot: Automated checklist: preflight ok, infra health OK, image v5.2 built, db migrations nop. Intended canary command: `deploy --tenant orion-labs --model v5.2 --canary 10% --monitor error_rate,latency`.

Luca Ferri: @Maya can we hold the ramp until we verify KV cache warmup metrics? Last run we saw ~600ms cold L5 latency on first requests which spiked tail latency. Prefer to start at 0% then cutover a tiny control group to warm caches.

Ryan Patel: Agree with Luca. Suggest: begin with 1% hit to a control slice for 10m, verify cache hit >80% and p99 < 400ms, then move to 10%. Also set automated rollback if error_rate > 1% for 5m or if p99 increases by >50%.

Product Ops: We also need the release notes and the pin for Private deployments. Orion is on an air-gapped Dedicated plan — they expect the pinned runtime SHA and a short changelog. Maya can you paste the pinned version?

Maya Chen: Pin: `runtime-sha: abcd1234-v5.2`. Release notes: fixed batching bug causing sequence misalignment, quantization kernel update for Ampere, improved prefix cache eviction. I'll paste the short changelog to the ticket.

Luca Ferri: If we're doing the tiny control group, can we add a quick canary policy: `route: control-slice -> 1%, warm-slice -> 9%`, with manual approval to proceed from 10% -> 50%? I don't want an automatic ramp until SRE gives thumbs.

DeployBot: Note: canary policy supports manual hold via `deploybot hold <thread_ts>`. Health checks enabled: latency, error_rate, model_mismatch.

Ryan Patel: I'll be oncall 17:30–19:30 UTC. I'll watch dashboards. If anything hits threshold I'll execute rollback and post summary. Also confirm that KMS rotation artifact creation for orion-labs completed at 15:10 UTC and keys are available — if not, we need to postpone.

Maya Chen: KMS rotation completed, verified with compliance. I attached the audit id in the ticket. Proceeding with the control-slice start plan. Go/no-go at 17:30 from SRE.

Product Ops: Orion legal slack confirmed they want a short maintenance blurb for customers: "We will be performing a brief canary rollout between 18:00-19:00 UTC; some requests may see a temporary increase in latency." I'll send the communication once SRE thumbs up.

Luca Ferri: One more ask — please pin the fallback model v5.1 config in the rollout so DeployBot can switch without config drift: `fallback: runtime-sha: ef56aa22-v5.1`.

Maya Chen: Done — pinned fallback in the canary runbook.

Ryan Patel: OK. Holding automated ramp. At 17:30 I'll check cache warmup and p99. If metrics are green, I'll reply `SRE: go` here and DeployBot can unhold and start ramp. If not, I'll reply `SRE: hold` and we'll reschedule to tomorrow 10:00 UTC.

DeployBot: Action queued: `hold` until manual unhold by @Ryan Patel. Reminder will fire at 17:25 UTC for final checks.

Maya Chen: Thanks team. I'll update the ticket with the canary commands and release notes. Ping me if you need rollback runbook edits. :thumbsup:

Ryan Patel: will do. Planning to run a dry check at 17:20 against synthetic traffic to validate warm-slice behavior.

Luca Ferri: Thanks — appreciate the synthetic run. If the warm-slice is OK then 10->50 manual ramp is fine.

Maya Chen: Copy that — see you at 17:30 for the go/no-go.
